stem:
Arachidonic acid is a fatty acid that is a common component of phospholipids.

Phospholipids can be used as a source of arachidonic acid when it is metabolised within cells in an enzyme-catalysed pathway known as the cyclooxygenase (COX) pathway.

The final products of the COX pathway can be different in different cell types, causing a range of responses. In some cells, the products are involved in the inflammatory response, which is a response by the body to infection. In other cells, cell division is stimulated.

Fig. 5.1 shows the **first reaction** in the COX pathway. This reaction is catalysed by an enzyme known as COX-2.

During an inflammatory response, compounds produced by the COX pathway cause an increased sensitivity to pain.

Some anti-inflammatory drugs are reversible competitive inhibitors of COX-2.

Fig. 5.2 shows how increasing arachidonic acid concentration affects COX-2 activity.
